title: a results page leaves the fetch step planned
line: a row of a FamilySearch results page fits the person whose 1950 fetch step was searched for by that name in that collection, so the run is found with the page and the row is a lead, never a card: his plan gets a fetch step for the row's own record; the listing points at a record and is not one, so the step stays planned and the row is not held, while the holder's run on the step's own fields keeps the search off the fetch list; a plan run keeps the step planned; a step standing done on a listing alone is planned again by the plan, one done on a record page stays done

steps.say: a 1950 citation on the person on the owner's word: the file cites the census on nobody in his household, so the step names the census as the file's own source record for it does (1,62308::0), with no record id of its own, the name the citation sits on as the file writes it, suffix and all

step.rationale: harness: a 1950 citation on the owner's word; fetch the record at United States, Census, 1950

expect.why: before the search is saved, the step's page is open for him

steps.say: the collection's search saved for the step: the first row is his, a lead; the listing is not the record

expect.why: read as a results page by its own markup; it fulfils the fetch step whose citation was searched for by this name in this collection, the citation's own suffix set aside so the surname compared is the surname searched; a row fits, so the run is found; the matcher proposes no row of a results page
no card at all: a results row is never one, and the rows that agree on the surname alone stay hints on the page

the first row fits him (his birth in Pennsylvania, the given name and surname, the year the index estimates): a lead on his plan, a fetch step for the row's own record at the holder of the results page, the row's words as its fields
one lead: the other nineteen rows fit him no better than the surname
the step's one log row: found, under the holder, the listing as its artifact, the query as run
a listing points at a record and is not one: the step stays planned
the row is not held on a listing
the holder answered the search on the step's own fields: the step's page no longer sends anyone to it
the row's own record page is the next page to save, listed under the record-page name with the ark filled in

steps.say: his plan run again keeps the step planned and logs nothing

expect.why: the citation is not held and the step was never done: nothing to plan again, nothing to close

steps.say: a second citation of the same collection standing done on the listing alone, as an earlier attach left steps

step.rationale: harness: a step an earlier attach marked done on a results page

log.note: harness: the listing's found run, as an earlier attach logged it

steps.say: the household's record page archived by its file name, the record a third step of the same citation is done on: a step done on it stays done

step.rationale: harness: a step done on the record page itself

log.note: harness: the record page's found run

steps.say: the plan: the step done on the listing alone is planned again, the one done on a record page stays done, the one never done stays planned

expect.why: one step planned again by this run
its only found run carries a listing that points at records: the citation is not held, so the step is planned again
the run stays as what happened; planning the step again writes no log row
its found run carries a record page: done it stays
